themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Treasury Secretary Bessent said on CBS Sunday that the government will look into Nvidia's chip sales to China and find out who oversaw compliance: "we do need answers" (Investing.com; Invezz). Huang and Nvidia's general counsel face House committees in early December. Separately, a TTM Technologies director bought about $292,000 of stock at 58.40 on Nov 20, the third insider to buy since Oct 28 (Form 4 via the dashboard).
themes.for_you: No chip entries. NVDA traded up about 6% premarket Monday, but a premarket move is not a close. TTMI insider buying is a reason to watch, not to buy: it sits under a falling 200 day (126.16) with no buy point.

themes.name: Space, Quantum and Cyber: Government Funded Frontier Tech
themes.what: CrowdStrike agreed Nov 23 to buy Zscaler in an all stock deal worth about $43.9 billion: 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share, about $260.41 on the Nov 20 close, a 34% premium. CrowdStrike also reported record net new ARR of $419 million and guided Q4 sales above estimates. Premarket, CrowdStrike fell about 8% to 9% and Zscaler rose 13% to 19% (8-K; Reuters via Globe and Mail; Seeking Alpha).
themes.for_you: No buys. CRWD has no buy point (lower highs and lower lows) and ZS closed 194.82, under its long term zone. All stock deals often weigh on the buyer until they close, because deal traders sell it. PANW is left out of both lists: consolidation can help or hurt it.

innovations.name: Defense and Security
innovations.what: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about $43.9 billion in stock (1.135 shares each, a 34% premium) and reported record net new ARR of $419 million. It is the largest security deal yet and fits the bottleneck in this file: the platforms with the most data are buying the rest. The stage stays early adoption.
innovations.for_you: No buys. CRWD fell about 8% premarket and has no buy point; ZS is under its long term zone. Avoid CRWD swings until deal selling settles.

innovations.name: Materials
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. The rare earth milestone in this file was out of date: China extended its pause on rare earth export controls by two months to Jan 10, 2027 (The National, Nov 9; SCMP). The separate gallium, germanium and antimony suspension still ends Nov 27, with no extension found as of Nov 23 (Fastmarkets). Licensing rules stay in place. No stage moves.
innovations.for_you: No action. Left out of both lists: a lapse on Nov 27 helps US processors on policy but raises costs for chip and defense buyers. MP and AA had range breaks lower this month; no puts on them.

countries.name: India
countries.what: Foreign investors bought more than Rs 1 lakh crore of Indian stocks in November, the first month over that mark, after six months of selling; analysts tie it to money leaving crowded AI trades and to cheaper oil (Business Today, Nov 19; IndiaIPO). INDA closed 52.90 on Nov 20, over its 52.13 range top on 10.8 million shares, 1.71 times its 50 day average, on a day the S&P 500 fell 3.7% (Massive).
countries.for_you: INDA's break is confirmed by her volume rule. It is a buy point on the dashboard (buy range up to 54.74, stop 50.90), not a swing setup. With the US market in a correction, wait for the S&P 500 to steady before any new entry.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI fell as much as about 5.8% to 4,586.80 on Monday Nov 23, after a 5.21% drop on Nov 20 to a 10 month low; Samsung and SK hynix led the fall. The government said it is preparing its market stabilization fund, unused since 2008 (Korea JoongAng Daily; Investinglive). Reports of the close differ: Invezz had a 3.31% loss after the fund news, others more than 5%.
countries.for_you: No Korea trades. EWY had a confirmed range break down on Nov 20 (2.17x volume), so no puts on it. Memory names in Korea fell even as US futures rose, a sign the AI selling is not over in Asia.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.what: Taiwan stocks rose about 2.1% on Monday Nov 23 as official buying and tighter short selling rules held up the market, while Korea fell (Invezz). The TSM ADR closed 318.71 on Nov 20, down 9.48% that day (Massive).
countries.for_you: No action. Government support can slow a fall but does not change AI demand. EWT had a confirmed range break down on Nov 19, so no puts. Left out of both lists: a supported bounce is not a trend.
